_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 344. While the pursuer is still on it the router is shoved south (to about y 680 by tick 440); once clear it flees north along the hill's west side (about (910, 611) at tick 560, (919, 386) at tick 680), every man clear of the hill, and rallies at tick 704 (ROUTING at 703, IDLE at 704) at about (924, 325), inside the clip (it ends at tick 720). Its anchor slides on north after the rally, to about (921, 295) by tick 710. The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill: the router's flight never meets it. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the pursuer's own deep column deforms: a 2-tick scan from the divergence (tick 343) reads a sustained shape residual of 148.1 wu against a 30 wu threshold, against 43.4 wu on the pre-#1739 merge-base; at this head the pursuer re-engages the router at tick 560 and swings round towards the south-east. Before the charge came straight in (rout at tick 469), the same scan from the rout read 75.4 wu: the straight charge did not cause the deformation. Because of it the declared checks pin the router's story beats with sparse post-rout samples (400, 560, 680, the rally at 703/704, and 710) rather than sampling the gallop densely. The pursuer's deformation, and the router's own post-rally overrun, are declared below as exemptions rather than sampled around.

shape_residual.reason: uid 1 (the pursuer): its own 80-mount deep column deforms after the rout. The latch and flight changes in #1739 act only on the router, but the router now gets away at its real pace: at tick 560 the pursuer, still on its ATTACK order against uid 0, re-engages it from a new angle, its facing swings from 61 to -112 degrees between ticks 558 and 578, and its anchor then backs away to the south-east to about (1090, 864) by tick 720. On the merge-base the pursuer trails the crawling router steadily with no swing. Sustained shape residual on a 2-tick scan from tick 343: 148.1 wu at this head against 43.4 wu on the merge-base (threshold 30). Tracked as a pursuer deforming on engaging a full-pace router in #1757, and by this clip's re-authoring in #1725. uid 0 (the router): after it rallies at tick 704 its anchor stops dead while its bodies still carry the flight, so they overrun their slots and the block re-forms on the move; sustained shape residual 218.2 wu at this head against 0 on the merge-base, where the router never rallies inside the clip. That is the post-rally overrun #1749 tracks.

overlap.reason: uid 0 (the router) closes up as its bodies overrun their slots on the rally at tick 704: closest body pair 3.654 wu at this head against the 5.0 wu floor, 40.0 wu on the merge-base, where it never rallies inside the clip. The post-rally overrun #1749 tracks.
